name: Sickle Cell S-Other Specified Hemoglobin Variant

criteria.description: Identification of hemoglobin S variant by hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Presence of vaso-occlusive crises or hemolytic anemia symptoms
Detection of specific hemoglobin S variant mutation by molecular genetic testing
Positive family history of sickle cell disease or hemoglobinopathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hemoglobin S variant confirmed by electrophoresis or genetic testing plus clinical features consistent with sickle cell disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other hemoglobinopathies and confirmation of the specific hemoglobin S variant.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sickled erythrocytes on peripheral blood smear

pathognomonic.notes: Episodes of severe ischemic pain due to microvascular occlusion
Ongoing destruction of red blood cells leading to anemia
searchTerms: long-term destruction of red blood cells
chronic anemia from red cell breakdown

common.notes: Enlarged spleen due to sequestration of sickled cells
Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera
searchTerms: yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown

common.notes: Reduced oxygen delivery due to anemia
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

common.notes: Painful swelling of hands and feet in young children
searchTerms: painful swelling of hands and feet

common.notes: Resulting from chronic anemia and hypoxia

occasional.notes: Pulmonary infiltrates with fever and respiratory symptoms
searchTerms: acute lung syndrome with chest pain
sudden chest pain and breathing trouble

occasional.notes: Cerebral ischemic events due to vaso-occlusion
Chronic non-healing ulcers on lower extremities

searchTerms: gallstones from red blood cell breakdown
stones in gallbladder from blood cell destruction

rare.notes: Elevated pulmonary artery pressure leading to right heart strain
Bone infarction causing joint pain and disability
searchTerms: loss of blood supply to femoral head

rare.notes: Vascular changes in the retina leading to vision impairment
Sudden pooling of blood in spleen causing acute anemia

laboratory: Presence of sickled red blood cells on peripheral smear
Positive hemoglobin S variant on electrophoresis or HPLC
imaging: MRI evidence of cerebral infarcts in stroke
X-ray or MRI showing avascular necrosis of femoral head
Chest X-ray showing acute chest syndrome infiltrates
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Response to sickle cell disease-specific treatments

distinguishingFeatures: Classic sickle cell anemia with homozygous HbSS genotype
More severe clinical course and earlier onset
Presence of hemoglobin C variant instead of S
Milder hemolytic anemia and fewer vaso-occlusive crises

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe bone pain indicating vaso-occlusive crisis
Acute chest syndrome with respiratory distress and hypoxia
references: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease. 2014.
